text: Numbertime is a BBC educational numeracy television series for primary schools that aired on BBC Two from 20 September 1993 to 3 December 2001. For its first four series, it was presented by Lolita Chakrabarti. El Nombre, an animated character used throughout the series, eventually became the concept for his own educational BBC children's television program; his name means "The Name" in Spanish, not "The Number", which would be "El Número". The third line of his opening song and his farewell catchphrase were changed several times during the series' run to reflect the focus of each series, though the original ones—("Writing numbers in the desert sand", used in the seventh series, and "Adios amigos, and keep counting", used in the fourth, sixth, seventh, eighth, and ninth series)—remain the most famous. In the second series, his tagline and farewell catchphrase were changed to "Drawing shapes in the desert sand" and "Adios amigos, and keep shaping up", respectively; in the third series, they were changed to "Righting wrongs in the desert sand" and "Adios amigos, over and out"; in the fourth series, his tagline was changed to "Counting numbers in the desert sand" (also used in the ninth series), and in the third episode of that series, his farewell catchphrase was changed to "Adios amigos, and fetch some water". In the fifth series, both tagline and farewell catchphrase were changed to "Telling time in the desert sand" and "Adios amigos, 'till the next time"; in the sixth series, his tagline was changed to "Using numbers in the desert sand"; in the eighth series, it was changed to "Counting money in the desert sand". The first series, aimed at four- to five-year-olds, had ten episodes focusing on numbers 1–10 in order. Each episode began with Lolita introducing herself, pulling the number from a string hanging from the ceiling, pushing it into its correct hole in a wall, and singing the main theme, "One to Ten", as each hole lit up. Between segments, there were comedy sketches based on nursery rhymes and fairy tales, animations featuring El Nombre, the Mexican gerbil who parodied Zorro, showing little Juan how to draw numbers while his four-piece mariachi band played "The Mexican Hat Dance" (with "Again!" after each performance), and a sequence encouraging viewers to spot things of the number of the episode—using the same video with a different number of items each time, accompanied by the recurring song "Numbers All Around", sung by a group of children. Each episode ended with Lolita singing a song or introducing an animation, followed by a challenge to find things related to the episode's number before she said she would "see them next Numbertime". The first series originally aired on Mondays as part of the Daytime on Two strand at 9:45 am, repeated at 2:00 pm on the same day; in Scotland, the 2:00 pm repeats were replaced with broadcasts of BBC Scotland's schools series Over the Moon with Mr. Boom. Episodes included the Narrator presenting Nursery Rhyme Theatre No. 1 – Little Miss Muffet with interruptions, and Little Jack Horner having one minute to find one plum on Sammy Sallow's game show, where success allows choosing a prize—either a mountain bike, a computer, or a picture of Sallow—ending with "One Finger, One Thumb, Keep Moving" sung by the children. The Narrator introduced Nursery Rhyme Theatre No. 2 with Marvo the Magician and his Two Amazing Dickie Birds, and Sammy Sport reported on Jack and Jill attempting to break the world record for running up a hill, filling a pail, and returning down in under two minutes; this episode ended with Lolita singing "The Animals Went in Two by Two". Sammy Sport joined Baa-Baa Black Sheep for the "Win a Bag of Wool" competition results, and Goldilocks invited viewers to Guess Whose House on Sammy Sallow's game show; the Numbertime Top Ten featured "Three-Sided Triangles" at No. 3, singing an original song titled "We're Triangles (Oh Yes We Are)". Farmer Giles introduced the finals of One Girl and Her Sheep, with Little Bo Peep and her dog Shep competing, and the Knave of Hearts conversing with the Queen of Hearts about her royal tarts; Lolita told viewers to "grab their partners and take the floor" as she introduced a quartet of dancing squares singing "Do the Square Dance". Australian chef Wally Bee and his assistant Bruce demonstrated how to cook five fat sausages on a barbecue for Barbecue Time, and Harry Headline visited the Five Pigs Family for Five Minutes' Fame; in the El Nombre sketch, Little Juan celebrated his fifth birthday, and the episode ended with Lolita singing "Fly, Little Dickey Birds, Round and Round". A gardener named Fred enlisted his family to pull up his enormous turnip for Garden Time, and Mr. and Mrs. Jones had to balance six eggs on a seesaw for Sammy Sallow's game show, with three attempts; the episode ended with Lolita singing "This Old Man" in voiceover. Sammy Sport traveled to Scotland to witness a fishing contest among the Seven Fat Fishermen to catch the largest fish on a bridge by the Clyde, and ordering seven portions of fish and chips caused trouble for the shopkeeper and his customer (who had seven children); the episode ended with Lolita singing "In My Little Garden, Now Promise You Won't Laugh" (also known as "One Potato, Two Potato"). Sammy Sport visited Shoeburyness to interview the Old Woman who Lives in a Shoe (who has eight children), and the Policeman asked viewers to help find Wee Willie Winkie for Crime Spot; it was evening in Little Juan's town in the El Nombre sketch, and the episode ended with Lolita imagining a world where everything was eight-shaped, visiting the Planet of the Eights to sing an original song—this was the only episode in which she did not wear her usual purple outfit but a silver spacesuit. Lucky the Cat recalled her nine lives on This Is My Life, and Harry Headline visited Miss Mary, Mary, Quite Contrary's garden for Garden Time, where he ruined her chances in the "Best Flowers Competition" and she ended up coming ninth; this was the only episode not to end with a song, instead featuring Lolita showing a homemade necklace with nine beads (three red, three blue, and three yellow), referencing the episode's third animated sketch. Farmer Giles and his dog Scruff demonstrated a new, quick method for mowing a meadow for Farming News, and Sammy Sport visited Ten Pin Alley to watch Ten Pin Pete attempt to become the new Ten Pin Champ; Lolita showed ten Russian dolls, and the episode ended with "Ten in the Bed", sung by the group of children who sang "Numbers All Around" earlier. Because this was the final episode, Lolita did not tell viewers she would "see them next Numbertime". In 1994, BBC Enterprises (now BBC Worldwide) released a video titled "Number Time" (BBCV 5359, spelled with two words), containing sixty minutes of edited highlights from the series (it was the only such release at the time); it was later rereleased in 1997 as the second half of a "two-on-one" video with "Alphabet Fun Time" (BBCV 5357), originally released around the same time and containing fifty-eight minutes of highlights from that show's 1992 series; the combined video was titled "Alphabet Fun Time and Number Time" (BBCV 5987) and rereleased in 1999. The series was later re-released in full as a "Video Plus Pack" in 1996, slightly altered to remove the episodes' opening titles. From 22 September to 1 December 1998, the BBC broadcast a "revised" version of the series as a lead-in to the sixth series; in place of Lolita, Bill (introduced in the fourth series) and Bernie (who joined in the fifth) introduced episodes with a number line, though Lolita's voice was still heard narrating reused animated sketches. All episodes except Numbers 1, 4, and 9 had the original live-action sketches replaced with the Dolls' House sketch (as in Series 5), though in episodes retaining original sketches, the prize scene in the "Find One Plum" sketch was cut and the "One Girl and Her Sheep" sketch was omitted. The El Nombre sketches were slightly lengthened, and sequences of children discussing the ten numbers (similar to those discussing time in Series 5) were introduced; although the Planet of the Eights sketch was reused, its vocal track was redubbed and Lolita was edited out. The "Numbers All Around" song by children was retained, but the "One Finger, One Thumb, Keep Moving" song had the children forming the number one and shouting its number cut at the end, and the "Ten in the Bed" song had a new video of the ten children in bed while retaining the original song. A lively maths series designed as a follow-on to the first series, featuring four colourful "clown-like" characters—Mo, Sappy, Grimble, and Jick—who live together. A robot named Trundle narrates each episode and helps them with maths. There are also animations and songs. The gang decide to have a barbecue, adding up sixteen guests and themselves to make twenty people; they learn to count in twos and fives, and Trundle shows a farmer using his sheepdog to count sheep. Trundle naughtily knocks over food boxes, which fall on Grimble and Jick, who rescue him but forget to send out invitations. It starts to rain, so they decide to restart the barbecue the next day. On a lovely day for a picnic, the gang learn about division by sharing food fairly—such as a quarter of a pizza, half a can of drink, or one banana each—though Grimble is upset, he is outshone by tapirs, tamarins, and wild horses shown at Marwell Zoo Park. Mo takes glass bottles to the bottle bank, leaving Grimble in charge of cleaning up and sorting by colour and shape; Trundle plays an odd one out game with the viewer at a Sainsbury's supermarket. When Mo returns, she sees the confusion and the group puts everything back in place. The gang learn about handling data when opening a pet shop; they try to ask people what their favorite animal is, but Sappy asks the right question without writing answers and Jick writes answers but asks the wrong question. Grimble goes out to find the correct data and discovers tigers are the world's favorite animal, so they close the pet shop. The gang learn about the number one hundred as they host a concert for one hundred people; they also learn to count in tens. Trundle shows that a hundred-year-old person receives a birthday card from the Queen, a century in cricket is one hundred years, and a centurion led one hundred Roman soldiers. He also shows how people count people in a football match, on a runaway train, and in a school orchestra. Sappy decides to conduct one hundred children. The gang learn that things are made to measure as Mo needs a shelf for her books, so Grimble and Jick build one but keep getting it wrong. Trundle shows two boys of different heights trying to set up goals, how goal widths vary in sports, and how the ancient Egyptians built pyramids using a cubit. The gang learn about weighing after Trundle receives a letter from a circus seeking a very light clown; the ringmaster assigns jobs to the gang to clear animal droppings, prepare hay, peanuts, and greens for Big Ears (thought to be an elephant), weighing them first on a seesaw and mixing custard pies without using scales. They discover Big Ears is actually a rabbit and are asked who among them is the lightest. The gang learn about measuring time as they prepare for Grimble's birthday; Mo and Sappy buy a green clock-shaped cake and a green alarm clock, and Jick makes a green jelly. Trundle shows Big Ben and explains how monks used sand clocks to ring the monastery bell and how ancient Romans used candles to measure time. The gang want to buy flowers and must first count their money and determine what they can afford; they are introduced to different coin denominations, combinations, and the concept that more coins do not mean a larger sum. Trundle shows a blind boy named Darren who identifies coins by touch. The gang are trapped in a board game called "Shape Master" and learn about 2D and 3D shapes; each finds a shape to escape—Mo finds a cube, Sappy finds a cylinder, Grimble finds a pyramid, and Jick finds a hexagon. Trundle explains how cubes and cuboids appear in buildings, how sticks of rock are made, and how shapes like hexagons, squares, rectangles, and diamonds tessellate. The second series, also aimed at four- to five-year-olds, had five episodes focusing on the four basic two-dimensional shapes. Each episode began with Lolita standing by a mobile with the shapes hanging from it, singing the main theme "Squares and Triangles, Circles and Rectangles" as the mobile turned. Once stopped, she walked to the nearest shape, asked viewers if they knew it, and it lit up when she named it—starting from this series, El Nombre had two sketches per episode: one showing Juan encountering that week's shape around town (with Juan being clumsy and facing villagers after El Nombre leaves), and the second showing him drawing it in the desert sand. The series featured four cut-out animated characters made from the shapes of the episode—circular man with magical powers, square robot with transformation powers, triangular knight with a magical lance, and rectangular man. In the final episode, they built a house together after the rectangular man built one from rectangles, and the square robot, triangular knight, and circular man transformed them into their own shapes. Each episode ended with Lolita singing an "extended" version of a song heard earlier during a montage of the shape in the real world (with the final one continuing over the credits), and viewers were challenged to find how many of that week's shape they could spot before the next episode. The first two episodes aired on Mondays at 9:45 am as part of the Daytime on Two strand, but due to May Day on 8 May 1995, the third episode aired the next day; the last two episodes aired on Mondays. In one episode, El Nombre shows Juan what a circle is (using a cart's wheel, a hoopla ring, a hoop with its stick), while Terry introduces the "Ring a Ring o' Roses Formation Dance Team" and their manager Cynthia, and a prehistoric couple attempt to invent the round wheel after square and triangular ones in Great Moments in History; in the second cut-out sketch, circular pawprints transform into a circular ladybird, circular bird, circular caterpillar (becoming a circular butterfly), circular fish blowing circular bubbles, circular car emitting circular smoke, circular man's head, and circular bear; in the CGI sketch, a circle gains two additional planes and transforms into a beach ball, a football, an orange, and the planet Earth. In another episode, El Nombre shows Juan what a square is (using Pedro and Juanita's frame, Señor Manuel and Señor Chipito's draughts board, The Maggot and Cactus saloon's sign, and a blackboard), while Bobby Cube asks the Shape Spotters on Let's Shape Up to name the square by pointing out its distinguishing features, and a square robot builds a square dog that turns on him after.

Terry introduces the world-famous "Ring a Ring o' Roses Formation Dance Team" (along with their manager, Cynthia) on Come Prancing, and a prehistoric couple attempts to invent the round wheel (after square and triangular ones) for their car in Great Moments in History; in the episode's second cut-out animated sketch, circular pawprints transform into a circular ladybird, a circular bird, a circular caterpillar (which becomes a circular butterfly), a circular fish that blows circular bubbles, a circular car emitting circular smoke from its circular exhaust, a circular man's head, and a circular bear; in its CGI animated sketch, a circle gains two additional planes and transforms into a beach ball, a football, an orange, and the planet Earth. El Nombre teaches Juan what a square is, using the then-unnamed Pedro and Juanita's frame, Señor Manuel and Señor Chipito's draughts board, The Maggot, Cactus saloon's sign, and a blackboard, while Bobby Cube asks the Shape Spotters on Let's Shape Up to name the square by highlighting its features; a square robot builds a square dog that turns on him after detecting his scent, but he scares it away by transforming into a larger square dog with a big square and running to and climbing up it; Jill Scoop reports on Old King Cole who wants his square bowl (after round, triangular, and rectangular ones) for Newsdesk; in the episode's CGI animated sketch, a yellow square in the bottom-right of a gameboard rises to become a cube with numbers 1–6 on its sides, which then transform into six groups of dots corresponding to those numbers as the cube becomes dice for Snakes and Ladders. El Nombre teaches Juan what a triangle is, using a musical triangle, a roadworks sign, and a stepladder, while Aladdin finds a lamp with a triangle on it (after those with a circle and square) for his Uncle Abanazer, but wastes three wishes (one for each side and corner) by turning Abanazer into a cat, himself into a mouse, and making the lamp disappear (causing Abanazer to turn on him, though both question why there was no Genie); a triangular knight attempts to slay a triangular dragon (burned the first time, rained on the second time when the dragon's fire is extinguished), and Bobby Cube again asks the Shape Spotters to identify the triangle by pointing out its features; in the CGI sketch, a triangle has a dotted line drawn inside it, folds up into a triangular-based pyramid, rotates to show numbers 1–4 on its sides lighting up, then unfolds back into a triangle. El Nombre teaches Juan what a rectangle is, using a plank of wood, the cart's side, and Pedro and Juanita's cardboard piece; Sammy Shape visits Old Mother Hubbard's cottage to find out "what makes a rectangle a rectangle" for Shapewatch (a spoof of Crimewatch), meeting her dog (who wants a bone but finds a rectangular biscuit instead); a rectangular man swims at a pool (after walking up a staircase, taking an elevator, and walking up another staircase), Humpty Dumpty identifies the shape of a brick in the wall he is sitting on (just before falling), and a woman named Jane writes a rectangular letter, posts it into a postbox with a rectangular slot and door, and receives it at her house. El Nombre helps Juan remember the shapes (using a square frame, a circular hoop with a stick, a rectangular book, and a triangular roadworks sign), while the rectangular man, square robot, triangular knight, and circular man (now with a circular body and a wheel for a foot) build a house together (after the rectangular man built one entirely from rectangles, and the others transformed them into their own shapes), showing that "all different shapes work well together"; Bobby Cube asks the Shape Spotters to identify the "Shy Shapes" in a cola can and a Battenberg cake; a rectangle folds into a hollow cylinder as two circles cover its ends and a second rectangle wraps around it to form a can of baked beans; in the episode's second El Nombre sketch, Juan draws "El Nombre" (a square, rectangle, circle, and triangle stacked) before drawing "the rope that hits him on the head and knocks him over"; El Nombre says it has never happened to him, so Juan swings a rope at him and tells him "It has now!"; the sombrero-less El Nombre chases Juan through the town to an extended version of his theme song (with the new tagline "Drawing shapes in the desert sand" at the end), but never catches him; this is the only old-style episode with just one live-action sketch. In 1996, both this series and the next were released on VHS as "Video Plus Packs" by BBC Educational Publishing (now BBC Active); the following year, they were rereleased together as a double "Video Plus Pack" named "Numbertime Shapes/Side by Side". After the 1997 corporate change, the BBC Education website (http://www.bbc.co.uk/education/) was superimposed onto the four shapes (a red circle, green triangle, yellow square, blue rectangle) at the end of this series' episodes and the next two series, but not the first series' episodes. The third series (aimed at four- to five-year-olds) has five episodes focusing on prepositions; each episode opens with Lolita singing "Under, Over, Everywhere" (with the previous series' mobile visible in the background, now with an apple, three stickmen, a rainbow, a cloud with a hot-air balloon, a sun, a snake, a spider, and a snail); Juan gains three new friends—Pedro Gonzales, Juanita Conchita, Maria Consuela Tequila Chiquita (Pedro and Juanita had previously appeared in the second series)—and a pet tarantula named Tanto; each episode ends with Lolita reciting a rhyme or singing a song (with the second episode's song being an extended version of one heard earlier in an animated sketch about a fox); a sketch in the second episode parodies EastEnders as "GreenGrocers"; this is the first series to credit the El Nombre voice actors at the end of its final episode (Sophie Aldred, Kate Robbins, and Steve Steen); although made in Autumn 1995, it was not broadcast until 28 February 1996. This series and the next aired on Wednesdays in the Daytime on Two at 10:25 am; this series premiered after a rerun of the second series, and the next series premiered after Daytime on Two returned following a two-week Easter break. Juan has no school concert activity, so El Nombre tells him to recite Incy Wincy Spider with Tanto; a bear flies a kite (which comes down in a tree, so he climbs it to retrieve it); a window cleaner is annoyed by her colleague's incompetence; Juan recites Incy Wincy Spider at the concert (but Tanto won't come down the drainpipe, so El Nombre coaxes him); three clowns named Boris, Doris, and Ethel compete to see who can raise the biggest laugh in Give Us a Giggle. Juan wants to take a photo of himself and Mama (but can't because he is behind the Polaroid); an engine driver pulls wagons (but the coupling snaps when going uphill, so when they roll back down, they are in front of him, and he must signal a second engine to help); Jack and Jill take Farmer Giles's horse and cart to market in Happy Ever After; a fox hides in his secret lair to escape a hunt (accompanied by a rhyme from Lolita in voiceover); Juan still cannot take a photo of himself and Mama (so El Nombre takes it and blows himself up in the process); the GreenGrocers proprietor tries to get his four customers to stand behind his stall and form a proper queue (until he is upstaged by a toy salesman). Juan cannot score past Pedro, so El Nombre (not in his usual outfit, but in what later becomes Santo Flamingo United's strip) tells him to kick the ball over him; Princess Perfect wants a bed that cannot have a pea under it; a tortoise named Toby goes to a party but cannot get over the hedge (unlike the bird, frog, squirrel, and rabbit, who all go over, but the last one tells him to go under); Pedro is on a stool so Juan cannot score past him (until El Nombre tells him to kick the ball under him, and when Pedro objects, they reduce the goal size, but El Nombre whispers to Juan to kick the ball to one side before Pedro leaves); the Cow (from Hey Diddle Diddle) is scared of jumping over the Moon (so the Little Dog volunteers the Dish instead, but suggests running under it). Mama wants to go to Hurrell's store but there is a hole in front (so El Nombre and Juan tell her to walk around it); a doll pushes three building blocks (numbered 1–3) together (but a clown driving a breakdown truck crashes into them, scattering them, so he must help rearrange them); Darren and Sharon Jam cannot decide where to place their new table on Lucky Lottery Winners; Mama comes out of Hurrell's store (but still thinks there's another way around the hole, so El Nombre tells her to jump across it if she is brave, but when he falls in, she chooses to go around it again); Lord and Lady Posh give instructions to their gardener, Jarvis, on where to plant their roses and daisies. Juan loses Tanto, so El Nombre helps him and Mama find him; the bear from the first episode tries to boil water in a saucepan but its bottom is missing; a magician turns a volunteer's watch and keys into an alarm clock and one big key; two burglars named Bob and Bert break into a sweet shop, eat all the sweets, grow too fat to escape through the window, and are caught by PC Nabb; from this point on, El Nombre returns to one sketch per episode (except in Episodes 21 and 26). The fourth series (aimed at five- to six-year-olds) has eight episodes focusing on "more than" (addition) and "less than" (subtraction); each episode opens with Lolita singing "More or Less" in a studio with pillars; this series introduces Bill (voiced by Paul Cawley), a green bird who can swallow and regurgitate almost any object whole; from the fifth series onwards, he is joined by a purple cat named Bernie (voiced by Laura Brattan), who appears at the beginning of each "revised" first-, sixth-, and seventh-series episode; the series also features a toad named Test who hops along the heads of fifteen multicolored people (wearing red jumpers with numbers 1–15) forming a numberline based on the episode's focus (their jumpers turn green when Test is on their heads); each episode ends with Lolita singing a song (the last one continues over the credits, and it is her final appearance, though she still says she will "see them next Numbertime"); two sketches in the first and seventh episodes parody Percy Thrower and Sir David Attenborough as "Percy Grower" and "David Attencoat"; a third sketch in the third episode parodies Surprise, Surprise as "What a Surprise" (with Cinderella receiving a surprise visit from her Fairy Godmother); the Bill sketches in the second and sixth episodes feature an enormous (unnamed) beetle who chases Bill after putting his feet into the eight wellingtons he regurgitates (in the second episode) and falls on top of him after pulling his last two wellingtoned legs off a wall (in the sixth episode); the fourth episode features a "female" version of Bill who falls on top of him after he shakes twenty mangoes off a tree; in the El Nombre sketches of the seventh and final episodes, Juan has his fifth birthday for the second time (this time, Pedro, Juanita, and Maria bring him an extra candle because he is one year older, so he ends up with eight), and El Nombre's town gains a female mayor, Señora Fedora, who is also a balloon seller. A little old woman, a little old man, and their little old cat enlist the help of the Little Old Mouse to pull up their enormous turnip for Growing Bigger; Little Juan needs to play two cymbals (not one); Test hops from 3 to 7; contestant Sharon plays Find One More to win two prizes; Bill adds four flowers together; Juan needs to hit the cymbals one more time (to make four hits); in the episode's second animated sketch, a slow butterfly tries to keep up with faster friends, but when he joins them on a tree, the branch breaks under their weight and they all fly away. Freda Fantastic from Fantastic Fairytales presents The Elves and the Shoemaker; Little Juan and El Nombre juggle seven of Mama's tomatoes (which they shouldn't play with); Test hops from 7 to 13; Fred Fantastic presents The Frog Prince; Bill adds eight wellingtons (belonging to an enormous beetle) which, when the beetle puts his feet into them, causes him to chase after Bill; in the episode's second animated sketch, Noah refuses to let a mammoth onto the Ark because there is only one of him, so he disguises himself as two bears with puppets and a tarpaulin, but is quickly discovered by Noah again. A ladybird's nine babies and three extra are saved from a fire (which is actually smoke from her husband Arnold's barbecue); Little Juan and his friends are about to have Mama's very hot chili with tacos but there are only three chairs; Test hops from 2 to 8; Fairy Godmother presents What a Surprise with surprising results for Cinderella; Bill puts twelve books on a shelf which collapses under their weight; in the episode's second animated sketch, a kiwi notices his (three-toed) footprints in the sand and tries to count them, but finds it too hard to count in threes and eventually runs away from the camera. Snow White goes to the Wild Wood Takeaway and gets seven Good Fairy Cakes (declining Grimbleshanks' first offer of Toad Burgers) for the dwarves' tea as it is Dopey's birthday; Little Juan accidentally blows Juanita's balloon up five more times, causing it to burst; Test hops from 1 to 11; Jack's mother will not let him climb the beanstalk as it only has ten leaves (it needs fifteen to change her mind); Bill shakes twenty mangoes off a tree, ending with a "female" version of himself falling on top of him; in the episode's second stop-motion sketch, a Tyrannosaurus Rex plans to eat a small Triceratops but is scared away when five larger Triceratopses, followed by five more, suddenly appear behind them to protect him. A magician makes six red balls disappear one at a time; Little Juan and his friends play musical chairs but all have a chair to sit on; Test hops from 12 to 8; Carlotta Bottle tries to sing Ten Green Bottles but the bottles "don't-a fall-a" because property master Reg is not present to knock them down; Bill eats three apples off a tree, causing the branch to break under his weight and the zero he was displaying to hit him on the head; in the episode's second animated sketch, three dogs wait to be picked by prospective owners at a pet shop (when only one remains, he does a dance with a hat and cane to pass the time). Rebecca Testament reports for Numbertime News and interviews Mr. Noah and one of his sons, Ham, who used to have only six animals on the ark (two elephants, two lions, two doves); Little Juan and Tanto go to get two melons for Mama's pie ("Melon Surprise") as a surprise, but Señor Manuel the greengrocer has to save two of his melons for a special customer; Test hops from 10 to 4; a woman wins two coconuts and then another two from a total of eight on a shy, Bill subtracts six of the enormous beetle's wellingtons (causing the beetle to fall on top of him); Little Juan discovers that Señor Manuel's special customer is Mama, who already has two melons; in the episode's second animated sketch, two monkeys.

Three apples fall from a tree, ending with the branch breaking under the weight and the zero displayed hitting the person on the head; in the second animated sketch, three dogs wait to be picked up by prospective owners at a pet shop, and when only one remains, he dances with a hat and cane. Rebecca Testament reports for Numbertime News, interviewing Mr. Noah and his son Ham, who previously had only six animals on the ark (two elephants, two lions, and two doves); Little Juan and Tanto go to get two melons for Mama's pie ("Melon Surprise"), but Señor Manuel the greengrocer must save two melons for a special customer, and later Little Juan discovers that the special customer is Mama, who already has two melons; Test hops from 10 to 4, a woman wins two coconuts and then another two from a total of eight, Bill subtracts six of the enormous beetle's wellingtons (causing the beetle to fall on top of him), and in the second animated sketch, two monkeys argue over two bananas and fall off their tree. The Early Bird loses all nine of his worms, and it is David Attencoat's fault for saying it isn't raining; Little Juan celebrates his fifth birthday for the second time, with more than five candles on his cake; Test hops from 11 to 5, Humpty Dumpty is afraid of heights so the crew removes the nine bricks of the wall three at a time, and Bill watches nine leaves blow off a tree before winter, ending with him being covered in snow; in the second animated sketch, three pegs blow off a washing line, three petals fall from three eight-petalled flowers (leaving five), a tricycle hits a stone and all three wheels fall off, three sides of a picture frame fall down (leaving one), and three mice steal three biscuits from a plate of eight (leaving five), one of whom returns with a note saying "Oh yes!" The magician from the fifth episode makes fifteen beads disappear under three beakers, five at a time; Little Juan nearly floats away with six of Señora Fedora's balloons, Test hops from 13 to 3, Simple Simon must find a penny for five of the Pieman's fifteen pies, which have all been sold to Old Mother Hubbard, Little Jack Horner, and the Queen of Hearts, and Bill recycles fifteen glass bottles (five green, five clear, five brown); in the second animated sketch, an enormous snail eats twenty trees from four gardens, scares away a smaller snail, a goat, a cow, and a flock of birds as it descends on each. In 1997, the series was released on VHS as a "Video Plus Pack" by BBC Educational Publishing, and on 16 May 2013 it was rereleased on DVD as a "DVD Plus Pack" by BBC Active with an accompanying teachers' book, though it is now out of print. The fifth series, aimed at four- to six-year-olds, had ten episodes focusing on time-related concepts, with Lolita no longer presenting; each episode began with an animated man with a pocket watch for a head, who also appeared in a musical sketch at the end of the sixth episode. El Nombre's town was named Santo Flamingo (first mentioned in the sixth episode in reference to their local football team, though the school sign read "San Flamingo School"), and Juan gained a new teacher, Constanza Bonanza; all but two episodes featured a rarely speaking man named Tim (played by Toby Jones) learning about time-related concepts, with his only spoken line being "Cook for half an hour" in the seventh episode when reading the instruction on a pie box. This series introduced the recurring sketch of the Dolls' House, featuring a cowgirl named Annie (Victoria Gay), a scarecrow named Scrap (Paul Cawley), a robot named Glimmer (Ashley Artus with a Geordie accent), a clock named Ticker (Mike Hayley), and from the sixth series onward, a butler named Branston (Brian Miller); they were frequently visited by a pirate named Captain Kevin (Roger Griffiths), on three occasions by a mechanic named Megamax (Fidel Nanton), Glimmer's girlfriend Princess Penelope (who visited Scrap when ill and ate all his chocolates), and a Russian ballet dancer named Nadia Nokoblokov (who performed Fryderyk Franciszek Chopin's Minute Waltz); in the seventh series, a detective named Shelley Holmes (Issy Van Randwyck) also visited frequently, though the sketch ended after that series. Although made after the BBC's corporate change in Winter 1997 (evidenced by the new logo at the end of episodes), it was not broadcast until 13 January 1998. This series and the next were originally aired on Tuesdays at 9:45 am as part of the Schools Programmes strand. In the first new-style episode, Tim wakes up in the middle of the night, brushes his teeth, and pours cornflakes but waits until morning for milk; Little Juan wakes up the village because he thinks a fiesta is in the morning instead of the evening; the residents of the Dolls' House take turns preparing meals, Bill takes a Polaroid of himself and new co-star Bernie (who comes in covered in mud, so she gives him a bath and takes another Polaroid); Bill gets covered in mud while trying to bathe her. Tim goes to referee a football match but the forecast is "windy," so he changes into his best suit; Little Juan has football practice but cannot remember the day; Bill decides to go on holiday to escape the rain, leaving Bernie with seven cans of cat food (one for each day of the week) and a can opener; Scrap and Glimmer argue over a teddy bear, and Captain Kevin resolves it. The newspaper in this episode's Tim sketch is dated before the BBC's corporate change (10 April 1997), but it incorrectly states that day was a Monday when it was actually a Thursday. Tim tries to put on his suit (jacket, trousers, hat, shoes, socks, tie) in the wrong order; El Nombre helps Mama make Delietta Smith's omelette with red and green peppers; Bill wakes Bernie for dinner but forgets the food; Scrap and Glimmer attempt to make a chocolate splodge cake for Annie. This is the first episode to refer to the Dolls' House by name. Tim grows two flowers and photographs them but cannot wait for the third; Pedro bets Juan he can find a spider faster than Tanto; Bernie wants an apple but cannot reach it, so Bill offers to fly up, but when he learns he can't, he challenges her to a tower-building contest; Megamax comes for tea, so Annie, Scrap, and Glimmer paint the house, but Glimmer runs down, and Megamax deduces he needs a new battery, giving him the "Max Pack Turbo Booster." El Nombre helps Little Juan learn about the clock face for homework; Scrap and Glimmer clean Ticker's spring; Bill trips over sleeping Bernie and flies into his clock, causing all numbers and hands to fall off; when he reassembles them with Bernie's help, the clock's cuckoo calls at 3:00 and causes him to faint. Little Juan and friends prepare for a school outing to see Santo Flamingo United play in the cup final at 3:00; Bernie naps at 2:00, but Bill plays a prank by moving the clock an hour ahead and replacing the cuckoo to wake her; Scrap waits for the postwoman to deliver his new "Scrap Jacket" (which he had been talking about all night, keeping Glimmer from sleeping). Tim (with his only line, "Cook for half an hour") cooks a big pie he bought, gets bored, and eats all his other groceries; Scrap is ill, so Annie asks Glimmer to take his temperature every hour and give him medicine every half-hour (but Princess Penelope visits); Bernie enjoys a "cattuccino" at the foot of a Big Ben-like clock tower until Bill bungee-jumps from its minute hand, steals it when he returns, drinks it, and returns the empty cup; Pedro, Juanita, and Maria agree to meet Juan for football at 2:30 (but Juan wonders how to know when it is 2:30). Tim has hiccups and tries to cure them by drinking water and holding his breath for ten seconds, but is interrupted by a crank phone call and a crank door-caller; San Flamingo School holds a three-legged race during its sports day; Bill and Bernie prepare to launch each other into outer space using only a seesaw; Nadia Nokoblokov visits the Dolls' House to help with her new dance (Fryderyk Franciszek Chopin's Minute Waltz). Tim receives a three-layered parcel at night (a birthday cake) with a musical birthday card playing a high-speed version of "Happy Birthday to You"; El Nombre helps Juan and Juanita order the four seasons correctly for homework (but they still need to draw a picture for each); Bernie puts a smile on a snowman (which turns out to be Bill) in winter, the snow melts and blossoms grow in spring, Bill waters flowers to help them grow and Bernie mows the lawn in summer, leaves blow off in autumn, Bernie throws a snowball at Bill and skates on the ice in winter, and puts another smile on a snowman (again, Bill); the residents of the Dolls' House also organize their clothes for each season (but Glimmer thinks they are being thrown away). In his last appearance, Tim is woken by a train, eats cornflakes, drinks coffee, and builds a house of cards, which falls when the last train passes; Ticker is broken because Annie, Scrap, and Glimmer failed to oil him, so Captain Kevin gives him a spare ship's bell; Bill and Bernie test each other's knowledge of time with their clock (Bill gets two wrong); Miss Constanza Bonanza, Pedro, Juanita, and Mama remind Juan that it is choir practice at 4:30, football practice at 5:00, tea at 5:30, and home at 6:00. The four shapes at the end of episodes were redesigned and differently colored (circle green, triangle yellow, square red, rectangle blue); in 1999, the series was released on VHS as a "Video Plus Pack" by BBC Educational Publishing. The sixth series, aimed at five- to six-year-olds, had ten episodes focusing on numbers 11 through 20; each episode opened with Bill and Bernie finding the episode's number on their number line (carried over from the 1998 revised version of the first series); Santo Flamingo gained an ice-cream seller named Señor Gelato, a carpenter named Señor Chipito (who previously appeared in the second series as owner of "The Maggot and Cactus" saloon), and a bandit named Don Fandango (who stole twenty gold coins from the bank managed by Señor Calculo in the final episode); former Blue Peter host Janet Ellis joined the El Nombre cast; although made in Winter 1998, it was not broadcast until 12 January 1999. Eleven soldiers (ten in two rows of five, the eleventh on the bottom) march around, ten form the number eleven; Little Juan and friends prepare for a second school outing to play football (but only have ten shirts, and El Nombre writes the episode number in desert sand); Scrap receives a "Soccerbox" football game from his great-aunt Laura Litterbin (which disappoints him as he dislikes football, and one of the eleven white players goes missing). In song, a pair of green slugs eat twelve plants (in three rows of four) and make the number twelve; Juan bets Juanita he can do more skips than her (mistakenly pronouncing her surname as "Chiquita"), and Pedro bets both that he can do more than either (counting as fast as possible); Captain Kevin does not want Branston to mention twelve because it reminds him of the final voyage of the good ship Rusty Bucket (when its crew found twelve biscuits). Thirteen balls (in three rows of four and one underneath) roll around; Mama told Juan and Pedro that Señor Gelato is having a lucky day and they must help him with thirteen lucky charms (but Juan initially thinks he wanted to help); Annie dances in the Dolls' House lounge (but Scrap does poorly if he had done thirteen steps). Fifteen cars (in three rows of five) go nowhere and no one cares; Señor Gelato accidentally drives his ice-cream tricycle into a three-legged table that Mama told Juan and Pedro to take to Señor Chipito for repair (they need a replacement wheel with fifteen spokes, but Juan initially thinks it has more as he cannot tell where he started counting); Scrap and Glimmer play marbles (Glimmer is losing badly, and his ten red marbles go missing). Seventeen windows (in four rows of four and one on the door) open on a building and lights switch on at night; El Nombre helps Juan, Pedro, and Señor Gelato collect all seventeen of Señor Manuel's tomatoes and put them in a bag; Scrap eats three lots of cake mix meant for three of twenty cakes for Captain Kevin's birthday party. A spaceship beams up twenty stars (in four rows of five) and beams them down again in the constellation of twenty; Don Fandango steals twenty gold coins from the bank (Tanto bites a hole in his bag, causing all to fall out); Nadia Nokoblokov visits the Dolls' House again to perform "The Dance of Twenty Turns"; Ticker realizes if he stays in the bedroom he does not have to watch, and Scrap eats a cake with twenty candles, so Annie and Nadia punish him by putting him on the revolving podium and telling Glimmer to make him do twenty "fast" turns; clips from the first and fourth series were reused in a musical sketch at the end of this episode. In 2000, both this series and the next were released on VHS as "Video Plus Packs" by BBC Educational Publishing; on 4 May 2012, this series was re-released on DVD as a "DVD Plus Pack" by BBC Active with an accompanying teachers' book and an audio CD (initially released as a cassette) — this one is still in print. The seventh series, aimed at five- to six-year-olds, had five episodes focusing on adding and identifying two-figure numbers up to 100; each episode opened with Bill and Bernie using a number square instead of a number line, joined by a caterpillar named Limo (voiced by Peter Temple) who crawls around to count the required numbers; in Santo Flamingo, Maria's sister Pepita Consuela Tequila Chiquita also started at San Flamingo School. This series, the last for the Dolls' House, was originally aired on Thursdays at 10:50 am as part of the Schools Programmes strand. Bernie stacks.

In 2000, both this series and the following one were released on VHS as "Video Plus Packs" by BBC Educational Publishing; on 4 May 2012, this series was re-released on DVD as a "DVD Plus Pack" by BBC Active, including an accompanying teachers' book and an audio CD featuring songs from the series (initially released as an audio cassette), which remains in print. The seventh series, aimed at five- to six-year-olds, consisted of five episodes focusing on adding and identifying two-figure numbers up to 100; each episode began with Bill and Bernie, whose number line was replaced by a number square, joined by a caterpillar named Limo (voiced by Peter Temple), who crawled around the square to count the required numbers. In Santo Flamingo, Maria's sister Pepita Consuela Tequila Chiquita also started at San Flamingo School. This series, which was the Dolls' House's final episode, originally aired on Thursdays as part of the Schools Programmes strand at 10:50 am. Bernie stacks twenty-nine plates (thrown to her by Bill) and does not know what comes after 29, so asks Limo for help; each time she adds ten more, she must ask again, but when she reaches 100, the plates fall over due to their weight. Scrap has lost all but one of his fifty buttons, so Shelley Holmes helps him find them, while Señor Gelato has only one cornet left and Juan volunteers to go to Hurrell's store to get twenty-four more, though he is later asked to bring three extra ones. While dusting the number square, Bernie sneezes out four numbers (18, 46, 69, and 83), and after Limo replaces them, she dusts Bill's beak, causing him to sneeze the entire number square over. Maria's sister Pepita also begins at San Flamingo School, which is seen for the first time in this episode, while Glimmer cooks apple pie and custard (using his Aunt Dimity's recipe), but Scrap has mixed up his cookbook and Limo must place four additional numbers (24, 38, 77, and 96) back into the square. Bernie takes a forty-wink nap, and Limo counts them by crawling along each row of the number square; Scrap is tired of licking envelopes (containing birthday party invitations), while Juan saves up money in his donkey bank and takes it to Santo Flamingo Bank, and Bill and Bernie ask Limo to find numbers 30 and 90 and add ten. Bill makes twelve sandwiches and ten iced buns for a party (and Bernie makes ten more of each, plus ten rock cakes each), while Scrap and Glimmer prepare party bags; Señora Fedora opens the 15th Annual Santo Flamingo Egg Festival and chooses Mama to make a giant omelette (requiring sixty-one eggs but only having twenty-one), and Bill and Bernie eat thirty of the party "goodies," but Bill drops ten buns and Bernie slides their remains into him, causing him to drop ten sandwiches; when they dance, he throws the remaining twelve into the air. Bill bought twenty packs of five fish fingers (but forgot the chips, as Bernie discovers when she puts them in the freezer), Glimmer paints a five-dot pattern, and San Flamingo School holds a jumble sale—this was also the final episode to feature the Dolls' House, even though it credits Victoria Gay at the end, she did not appear as Annie in this series. The eighth series, aimed at five- to seven-year-olds, had ten episodes focusing on coin recognition, money problems, coin equivalents, and change (previously covered in BBC's Numbers Plus and Megamaths); each episode opened with eight "money-spiders" (one for each coin: 1p, 2p, 5p, 10p, 20p, 50p, £1, and £2) descending from a tree. This series introduced pounds and pence to Santo Flamingo, added a railway station named El Loco and a pizza delivery boy named Leonardo de Sombrero, and reworked the recurring song "Numbers All Around" to focus on coins. It also introduced the recurring sketch Screensaver, featuring a screen named Screen (voiced by Sue Elliott-Nicholls), customers (all played by Michael Fenton-Stevens), and a robot named T1L (pronounced "Til," voiced by Paul Vates). This series aired on each day of the working week for a fortnight as part of the Schools Programmes strand at 11:05 am. Juan, Mama, and Pedro go to the fair (but don't know if they have enough money for the coconut shy, roundabout, or candy floss), Bill runs a cake stall but Bernie can't decide whether to buy one, so flips four coins (1p, 2p, 5p, 10p) into the air—though they don't come down again—and a cricket player wants to buy glue from Screensaver to fix his broken bat. San Flamingo School holds another jumble sale (to raise money for a new school bell), Bill now runs a drink stall but closes after selling his last drink to Bernie for 8p, and Bernie disguises herself as a vending machine to trick Bill into giving her money back; a policeman wants to buy a timepiece from Screensaver (who try to sell him Big Ben for 10p). Little Juan and his friends visit Santo Flamingo National Park to see the Giant Cactus, while Bill runs an "everything" stall (but when Bernie collects 10p from a 5p, two 2p, and a 1p coin, she misinterprets "everything 10p" and wheels it away), and a sailor wants to buy a cake from Screensaver (who offer a wedding cake). Little Juan and his friends arrive at the park and see the Giant Cactus, while Bill and Bernie buy a snack (5p), juice (2p), and chocolate (3p) from three talking vending machines; an old man wants to buy a new wheel for his wheel-basket from Screensaver (they try to sell him a bicycle wheel). Juan and Maria notice Señor Manuel has set up a giant jellybean machine outside Hurrell's store, Bernie plays "Coin Sports" and loses Bill's 1p, 2p, 5p, and 10p coins after they roll into a river (totaling 18p), and a Russian secret agent wants to change his appearance at Screensaver (they sell him a Hawaiian shirt for 4p, a blond wig for 8p, and a striped bow tie for another 8p). Mama takes Juan back-to-school shopping at Hurrell's store (and has him try on a hat that is too big), Bernie pays 20p for an elephant ride and gets 5p change (finding it slow, she pays another 20p for a rocket ride and gets another 5p change, then masquerades as a cat ride to trick Bill into giving her a third 5p; after he gives it to her, he wants to do it again, but she is too tired to), and a chef wants to buy butter and eggs from Screensaver. Señor Gelato promises Juan and Juanita ice cream if they go to Santo Flamingo Bank and exchange 50p for coins, while Bill and Bernie try to exit a car park (when Bill collects 50p, the barrier catapults him into the air), and a businessman wants to buy a pet from Screensaver (they sell him a "Starpet" from their home planet for 50p). Miss Bonanza is getting married (and Juan organizes the school's 50p collection for her gift), Bill pays 50p for a photo and gets 20p change (but the booth takes it before he can enter, so Bernie pays another 50p and Bill counts her change; when she looks out, the booth takes a photo of her tail, so they combine their changes to have a joint photo), and a rock star wants new shoes from Screensaver (they sell him blue suede platforms for 15p each). Pedro, Juanita, and Maria sleep over at Juan's house (planning to watch a scary film), while Bill and Bernie do laundry (paying 10p for washing powder and £1 for the machine); when Bernie inserts a £1 coin into the washing powder machine, she gets ten cups, which she pours into the washing machine, causing it to spew foam over the floor. A cowboy named Tom ("Big T") wants to buy a shirt with a big T from Screensaver. Little Juan performs a concert to raise money for the school bell (with Don Fandango masquerading as Mama and trying to steal all his £1.60 earnings), while Bill and Bernie want to go on a boat trip for £2 (though Bernie has a £2 coin, they both have to go back so Bill can gather the coins; when they return, Bernie gets on the boat before it leaves, but Bill is not lucky—he carries all his coins in a giant sack). A non-speaking clown tries to get Screen and T1L (in their last appearance) to guess he wants a top hat (50p) and a rabbit (for £1.50) at Screensaver. In the ninth (and final) series, aimed at six- to seven-year-olds, ten episodes focused on adding and subtracting, similar to the fourth series (without Lolita, live-action sketches based on nursery rhymes, or Test the Toad); Numbertime News, which had appeared in five episodes of the first series with Sammy Sport (played by Andy McEwan, who had played Matt Dillon in Death Without Dishonour, episode 26 of Taggart), and one episode of the fourth series with Rebecca Testament (played by Issy Van Randwyck), became a recurring sketch, with anchorwoman Tara Boomdeay (played by Elisabeth Sladen, who had played Sarah Jane on Doctor Who and several characters in episodes of the third and fourth series) and roving reporter Brad Quiff (played by Ian Connaughton). This series saw Michael Fenton-Stevens return to join the El Nombre cast and introduced Addem (voiced by Richard Pearce), a green snake who discovered the series' concept with a yellow ant named Ann (voiced by Moir Leslie) and a whole civilization of multi-coloured ants (mostly voiced by Brian Bowles and Richard Pearce, with the Queen Ant voiced by Moir Leslie). The series originally aired on Mondays at 11:05 am, but 1 October 2001 was the first day of the Labour Party Conference, so its fourth episode was not shown until the following week. Brad Quiff investigates addition (with the "High Peaks Climbing Team"), Bernie challenges Bill by giving him numbers to add to make twenty, Addem discovers a civilization of ants (headed by Ann), and Little Juan enters a competition on Radio Flamingo. Juan and Pedro go shopping at Señor Calculo's barbecue, Bernie plants seeds in window boxes and Bill helps her add them, Brad Quiff investigates how many chocolate bars the Malarkey Gang have stolen and Ann must get twenty-nine ants into three houses. Addem helps Ann sort beds for the "adolescants," Little Juan faces Don Fandango in the final of the Santo Flamingo Darts Championships, Brad Quiff reports on the popularity of the "Princess Patsy" doll, and Bill and Bernie wash their socks at the launderette from the eighth series. Brad Quiff visits a country fair to meet bun makers, El Nombre reads Little Juan a bedtime story (about Don Fandango robbing the Santo Flamingo Bank), Ann needs to prepare twenty-five meals for the "Accounts Department," and Bill and Bernie try to make carrot juice. Ann learns about adding acorns in hundreds, Brad Quiff reports on the opening of the "Whizzo Lolly Factory," Bill helps Bernie count her pennies as she plans to "shop 'till she drops," and Juan and Pedro earn pocket money by picking lemons for Señor Manuel. Brad Quiff reports on an American football team passing the ball down a numberline, Bernie challenges Bill again by giving him numbers to subtract to leave ten, a pair of cowboy ants must take twenty-seven aphids to the milking shed, and Juan goes on holiday to Costa Fortuna with Mama, Pedro, Juanita, and Maria after winning the first episode's competition. The Queen Ant decides to hold a regatta, Juan and his party board the plane to Costa Fortuna, Bill washes more socks at the launderette but Bernie tells him to separate whites from coloureds, and Brad Quiff reports on crowds gathering for Punch and Judy performances all day; in this episode's adaptation of the story (also frequently adapted by Mr. Partridge on Hi-de-Hi!), Mr. Punch steals Judy's marbles while she is asleep. Brad Quiff reports on an annual tug-of-war contest between the Diddletown Dodgers and the Softville Saints, Ann needs eighty-two candles for the Queen Ant's birthday cake, Juan and his party arrive at the Sea View Hotel in Costa Fortuna (where they meet guide Pablo), and Bill and Bernie insert two 20p coins into two of the three talking vending machines from the eighth series to buy a snack (16p) and juice (14p), receiving 4p and 6p change respectively; they combine their changes to buy a bar of chocolate (10p) from the third machine. This is one of only two episodes with an El Nombre sketch not set in Santo Flamingo. Juan and Pedro go to the fair in Costa Fortuna (where their guide Pablo fronts a ring-toss game), Ann must fill forty-five places in the "Accountants'" new building, Bill runs an apple stall (but when Bernie wants to buy three, he has none, so they both pick some from an apple tree), and Brad Quiff reports on "Doreen's Sweet Shop" being robbed of a large pile of chocolate eggs. In the show's final episode, a squad of 100 marching ants keeps breaking up and reforming, Juan and his party return to Santo Flamingo (and are told at customs they can only bring a certain amount), Brad Quiff reports on the "Numbertime News Live Formation Climbing Team" (who show a trick to remember sums), and Bill and Bernie have tea (Bill puts ten sugar cubes in his, and when Bernie asks what he is doing, she makes him forget how many he added); even though this was the last episode, El Nombre received a second series in 2003. In 2001, by which time VHS was becoming obsolete, this series was released on VHS as a "Video Plus Pack" by BBC Educational Publishing. In 2002, by which time VHS was even more obsolete, this series was again released on VHS as a "Video Plus Pack" by BBC Educational Publishing. The first series was accompanied by a ten-part radio series on BBC School Radio entitled Radio Numbertime, focusing on numbers 1–10 in order, which aired from 21 September to 30 November 1993. Another radio series, simply titled Numbertime, aired on BBC School Radio from 29 September 2000 to 26 March 2003, and a third radio series, again titled Numbertime, aired from 1 May to 26 June 2014.
From 29 September 2000 to 26 March 2003, a third radio series titled Numbertime, matching the name of the previous defunct television series, was aired on BBC School Radio from 1 May to 26 June 2014.
